What you need to film an amateur football match: equipment and costs

24 November 2026 · Kadar

Clubs often put off filming their matches because they think it needs a camera, a laptop and someone who understands both. It does not. Most of what you need is already in somebody's pocket. Here is the list, in the order in which it matters.

1. A phone

A phone from the last few years films better than the camcorders clubs used a decade ago. Use the main camera on the back, clean the lens, and free up storage before the match: ninety minutes of video take several gigabytes.

2. A tripod, the one thing you must buy

A steady picture is the difference between a broadcast and a shaky video. A simple tripod with a phone holder costs about as much as a match ball. A taller one, around two metres, is worth the extra money because height lets viewers see over the players nearest to you.

3. Power

Filming and streaming at the same time empty a battery within one match. Take a power bank and a cable long enough to reach from the tripod's foot to the phone. Plug it in before kick-off; do not wait for the warning.

4. Mobile data

If you only record, you need no connection at all. If you stream, count on roughly 1 to 2 GB an hour at 720p. Check the signal where the tripod will stand, and ask whether the clubhouse Wi-Fi reaches the touchline: often it does not.

5. The app that draws the scoreboard

Kadar turns the phone into a small broadcast desk: the scoreboard and the clock are part of the video, and you keep the score with large buttons. Streaming to YouTube or Facebook with the scoreboard and recording to the phone are free.

Worth adding later

  • A second phone for a colleague who keeps the score from the bench, while you watch the picture.
  • A rain cover or just a clear plastic bag and a rubber band. Matches are not cancelled for drizzle.
  • An external microphone if you want commentary. Without commentary the phone's own microphone picks up the ground well enough.
  • A small platform or a step ladder if your ground has no stand.

What it adds up to

For a club that already has a phone, the first season costs a tripod and a power bank. That is less than one set of training bibs, and a sponsor in the picture can pay it back in a single match.
